messages:
Jordan: Heads-up — we're seeing 3x tail-latency spikes on private cluster A (us-west) after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak + batching heuristic change. Spikes correlate with NAT burst events from tenant T-42. Dumped pcap and kernel logs below, /cc @Maria @Kevin

Maria: On it. Do you have a small pcap excerpt and the exact ks commit?

Jordan: pcap excerpt (trimmed):
```
17:42:12.123 IP T42->ext: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12405, ack 54321, win 65535
17:42:12.124 IP ext->T42: Flags [.], ack 12405, win 16384
(repeated bursts ~200pps for ~30s)
```
and dmesg tails: `kernel_selector: chosen=opt_path_v3 latency_us=2400` then lots of `kv_cache: eviction rate=0.32` lines.

Kevin: Two quick suspects: conntrack exhaustion under NAT burst + MTU/fragmentation oddness at the customer's firewall. If their firewall is fragmenting packets we get more syscalls per request and conntrack pressure. Seen this before with DF/DF=0 behavior.

Anya: I'm oncall — I just scaled NAT pool + bumped conntrack_max to 500k on cluster A and added a temporary iptables rule to drop malformed fragments.
Command run: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=500000` and `iptables -A PREROUTING -t raw -m frag -j DROP`
Latency improved to baseline for ~10m then we saw another spike.

Samir: Can we pin kernel selection back to previous behavior while we investigate? If the kernel path increases context switches it could amplify KV cache thrash.

Jordan: We can pin — staging has `ks-v2.7.1` which predates the selection change. Also notable: during spikes `kv_hit_rate` fell from ~98% to ~70% and `batch_size_mean` dropped from 48 -> 12 (so more syscalls per token).

Maria: Proposal: enable sticky routing for tenant T-42 to route their flows to dedicated NAT nodes to avoid noisy neighbor effects, and revert the new batching heuristic that aggressively reduces max batch size under certain latency signals.

Kevin: I've applied sticky route for T-42 -> nat-dedicated-03 and adjusted egress firewall MTU clamp to 1452 on nodes behind that route. conntrack usage dropped and tail-latency improved ~40% within 5m. :+1:

deploy-bot: rollout pinned `ks-v2.7.1` to cluster A at 1972345978 — finished.

Anya: After pin + sticky route, latency stable but KV cache eviction rate still elevated (evictions/sec ~120). Jordan, can you share profiler output? Might be a scheduling change in the chosen kernel path causing more preemptions.

Jordan: Pasted top of flamegraph (trimmed):
```
kernel_sel_update()  45% cpu
  batch_pack()      30%
    kv_lookup()     20%
    syscall_write() 10%
```
Hypothesis: the chosen kernel path favors an I/O-oriented codepath that reduces max batching to keep p99 low for small requests, but with noisy high-throughput tenants it causes batch fragmentation + KV thrash.

Samir: Action items agreed: (1) keep sticky route for T-42 for 24h, (2) pin ks to v2.7.1 on cluster A until we validate fixes, (3) revert batching heuristic in next canary, (4) increase kv_cache size by 20% on cluster A and tune eviction_policy to lru_adaptive. I'll open an incident doc and schedule a short postmortem.

Maria: Also note for PM: we should proactively notify customer T-42 that we applied a noisy-neighbor mitigation (sticky routing) and are investigating root cause.

Jordan: Thanks all. Quick metrics snapshot (pre/post):
`p50: 12ms -> 14ms (minor), p95: 48ms -> 160ms (spike), p99: 120ms -> 480ms (peak)`, after mitigations p95 down to ~90ms.

Anya: I'll monitor for 6 hours and escalate if spikes recur. If anyone sees recurrence, re-open thread and ping @Samir. :eyes:

Jordan: Filing attachables and logs to the incident doc — will link in the postmortem. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
